The Karnataka government has sanctioned the prosecution of suspended IAS officer Gyanendra Kumar Gangwar , former Controller of Examinations of the Karnataka Public Service Commission (KPSC), in connection with the alleged question paper leak in the Veterinary Officers’ recruitment examination. Gangwar is accused of misusing his official position to leak question papers and answer keys to middleman Basavaraj Kannale a day before the examination, allegedly facilitating malpractice in the recruitment process. Investigators allege Kannale collected ₹1.5 crore from candidates for leaked exam material, including ₹1.30 crore allegedly paid to Gangwar as illegal gratification. Some candidates were reportedly taken to a Bengaluru outskirts resort to memorise answers before the exam. Gangwar, earlier suspended and held in ED custody, now faces criminal proceedings following prosecution sanction over alleged bribery, exam leaks and recruitment irregularities. — BMB 
 Auto fare fight ends in advocate’s murder 
A 46-year-old city-based advocate was allegedly murdered following a dispute over an auto-rickshaw fare in Annapoorneshwari Nagar police station limits on October 9. Initially suspected to have died of cardiac arrest, his death was confirmed as murder after a post-mortem examination revealed fatal head injuries. Sriram V was allegedly assaulted by auto-rickshaw driver Prithviraj, 31, who has been arrested. Police said the two argued over the fare near Ambedkar College after Sriram refused to take the auto and continued walking. Prithviraj allegedly followed him with associates, abused and assaulted him on the head before fleeing with his mobile phone and cash. Sriram later collapsed and was taken to a private hospital, where he died around 3pm. Doctors initially suspected cardiac arrest, but his family raised doubts after noticing injuries. A post-mortem found blood clots in his head, confirming fatal injuries and leading police to register the case as murder. — BMB 
 Flash fire at godown leaves three injured 
Three people, including a nine-year-old boy, sustained burn injuries in a suspected LPG cylinder leak and flash fire at a godown in Rajarajeshwari Nagar (RR Nagar) on Saturday morning. The injured have been identified as Bablu, a native of Bihar, his neighbour Lakshmamma and a minor boy. Police shifted all three to a nearby private hospital, where they are undergoing treatment. According to local residents, Bablu, who has lived in Bengaluru for nearly two decades, runs a pani puri business. Although he resides elsewhere in the city, he uses the RR Nagar premises as a storage facility and preparation unit for his vending carts. 
 Preliminary investigations suggest that an LPG cylinder may have leaked overnight, allowing gas to accumulate inside the closed premises. The gas is suspected to have ignited when Bablu arrived in the morning and opened the entrance, triggering a flash fire that sent flames bursting onto the street. Bablu suffered burns, while Lakshmamma and the boy, who were outside the premises, also sustained injuries. Fire and emergency personnel, along with police, rushed to the spot and brought the situation under control. Officials inspected the premises and are investigating the cause of the fire. — BMB 
 Delhi man held over ‘spurious sting’ video 
The Central Crime Branch (CCB) has arrested Delhi-based Ritesh Pandey for allegedly uploading a video linked to a purported sting operation targeting former Karnataka Chief Minister Siddaramaiah on social media. Investigators suspect that Pandey was instructed to upload the footage by a person associated with the social media team of a regional political party. He was brought to Bengaluru for questioning, and his mobile phone was seized. The probe reportedly revealed that Pandey used a second-hand SIM card and an eSIM-enabled device to download the video from a pen drive and upload it online. The CCB is examining the device and digital evidence to trace the footage’s circulation.
Investigators are trying to identify the person who handed over the pen drive and establish the roles of others allegedly involved. Several people have been summoned for questioning based on information provided during the investigation. Pandey was granted bail and directed to cooperate with the probe. CCB had earlier questioned private news channel head Rakesh Shetty, who was released on anticipatory bail. Investigators are tracing the video’s source and circulation. — BMB 
 Twin chain snatches lead to three arrests 
Police have arrested three persons in two separate chain-snatching cases reported in the Southwest Division, recovering gold ornaments worth a total of Rs.5 lakh and a two-wheeler allegedly used in one of the crimes. In the Talaghattapura case, the suspects were arrested within 36 hours of the crime. On October 21, two men allegedly pushed a pedestrian in Lingadheeranahalli and snatched a 15-gram chain worth `2 lakh. Police arrested both in Turahalli, recovered the chain and seized their motorcycle. A court remanded both to judicial custody. Kumbalgodu police arrested a suspect on October 22 for allegedly snatching a 40-gram mangalsutra worth Rs.3 lakh near Challaghatta bus depot. Police recovered it from an Uttarahalli jewellery shop on October 23 and secured seven days’ custody. — BMB GALLERIES View more photos Aero India 2021: 13th edition of air show begins today
